text:
harper: short follow-up from the canary retro: we still lack a crisp precedence model for automatic fallbacks during A/B. want to nail ownership, cooldowns, and telemetry before next run.
ryan: agreed. my take: runtime can perform an immediate protective action for safety but must post an immutable event and attempt to acquire a short-lived lease. orchestrator is the authority for sustained changes.
isabel: lease sounds good. runtime should not be allowed to flip indefinitely without orchestrator acknowledgement. lease fields: lease_id, granted_by, start_ts, ttl_s, priority, reason_code.
meera: add a fallback_level enum too so downstream tooling knows severity: NOOP, SOFT, HARD, BLOCK.
harper: good. what about noisy signals causing thrash?
Tony: (typo fix) tony: two-tier cooldown: local debounce (20-90s) to avoid flip-flop from sample noise, plus cluster lease TTL (5-30m) enforced by orchestrator. runtime may request shorter ttl but orchestrator can extend.
isabel: also propose a burn-in rule: for the first N minutes of any canary, runtime only emits INFO events. ACTIONABLE events need a quorum across instances (e.g., 3 instances across zones) to be actionable. prevents single-instance flaps.
ryan: quorum by AZ is key. implement quorum detector in orchestrator: collect events per-cohort, group by az, require >=M azs with >=K instances reporting ACTIONABLE in window W.
meera: telemetry schema (flat json-lines): cohort_id, decision_id, lease_id, source, fallback_level, reason_code, actionability, score, p50_ms, p95_ms, error_rate, samples, ttl_s, notes. keep it compact.
harper: reason_code enum suggestions: LATENCY_P99, SERVE_ERRORS, KVS_LAG, OOM, MODEL_CONFIDENCE_DROP.
Tony: add an actionability enum: INFO, ACTIONABLE, CRITICAL. runtime only auto-acts on ACTIONABLE/CRITICAL. INFOs are for visibility.
isabel: interface question: should orchestrator push decisions via a push RPC or via configuration poll? i'd prefer push (gRPC) for fast emergency overrides, but it must be authenticated and rate-limited.
ryan: push + idempotency + audit trail. RPC: SetFallback(decision_id, cohort_id, fallback_level, expiry_ts, actor) returns ack. require mTLS and a signed token from orchestration control plane.
meera: also include a read-only endpoint runtime -> orchestrator for lease status: GetLease(decision_id) so runtime can reconcile if async grant happens.
harper: long-term thought: move short-lived lease ledger into a tiny local agent that persists ephemeral state and syncs via a write-optimized kv. avoids overloading central etcd for every small canary.
Tony: agree. short-term: central orchestrator leases persisted in etcd with sharded keys by cohort hash to avoid hotspots.
isabel: simulation and testing: must build a harness to replay traffic + inject latency/error modes and verify decisioning path: runtime preempt, lease requests, quorum evaluation, orchestrator overrides, and cooldown enforcement.
harper: action items: (1) isabel + ryan: draft lease proto + SetFallback/GetLease RPCs by Tue (2) meera: telemetry json-lines schema PR by Wed (3) tony: implement a small lease TTL sharding plan + ops cost estimate by next week (4) ryan: simulation harness skeleton for smoke tests.
meera: small note: decision_id format should be deterministic and traceable: e.g. unixms-cohort-rand. store it in telemetry and in the lease record.
ryan: also we should emit a compact "why" tag for faster SRE triage: one-liner reason_code + optional link to logs.
Tony: ops-bot: canary started service=router rev=canary-b3 at 2026-05-02T09:12Z.
devops-bot: alert: elevated fallback-rate detected for cohort=canary-b3 zone=us-west-2 at 09:14Z.
harper: ok, keep changes minimal for this cycle: prefer conservative thresholds for canaries. we'll iterate on lease semantics after simulation results.
isabel: noted, i'll include burn-in/quorum text in the proto doc.
meera: i'll open the telemetry PR with example log-lines.
ryan: good session. tag follow-ups in RFC.
harper: thanks all. closing thread.
